name: Tyndall's ribbon of invisible heat
scope: The Victorian bench experiment that found WHICH gases trap Earth's warmth. T1: in 1859 at the Royal Institution in London, John Tyndall filled a long tube with a gas, shone invisible heat through it from a lampblacked copper cube of boiling water, and asked what got through -- dry air, oxygen, nitrogen and hydrogen let the heat sail straight down the tube as if it were empty (the hook: the gases that make up 99% of the air barely notice Earth's outgoing heat). T1/T2: the whole readout was a thermopile wired to a galvanometer -- a needle swinging on a scale; a gas's grip on heat showed up as a KICK of the needle. T2: the gas that stunned him was WATER VAPOUR -- a trace of it absorbed enormously more heat than the entire bulk of dry air, and Tyndall concluded that water vapour, not carbonic acid, is Earth's dominant heat-trapping gas (the bank states this ranking plainly). T3: carbonic acid gas (CO2) and ozone also absorbed strongly while oxygen and nitrogen did not -- Tyndall's pattern was that simple two-atom molecules were transparent while compound molecules absorbed; a molecule has to be able to FLEX in a way that shifts its charge to grab infrared (teach the mechanism before testing it). T3: the woman who got there first with a cruder tool -- on 23 August 1856 at the AAAS meeting in Albany, Eunice Newton Foote's paper was read aloud by Joseph Henry of the Smithsonian: two glass cylinders, thermometers, sunlight, and the finding that the cylinder of carbon dioxide 'became itself much heated' and took 'many times as long in cooling'; published that September in the American Journal of Science and Arts. T4: the honest difference between them -- sunlight in a jar mixes incoming sunlight with outgoing infrared and cannot separate them; Tyndall's tube tested INFRARED alone, which is the actual greenhouse mechanism. Give Foote the credit she earned and state the difference. T4: what Tyndall proved and what he did NOT -- Joseph Fourier had argued in the 1820s that the atmosphere retains heat; Tyndall supplied the missing WHICH, presented in his Bakerian Lecture to the Royal Society on 12 December 1861, and never computed a temperature for the planet. T5: the same physics is in a school corridor today -- every non-dispersive infrared CO2 sensor and every hospital capnograph works by measuring exactly the absorption Tyndall measured, which is why this is the firmest fact in the whole climate argument: it is re-measured commercially, every day, by instruments that would stop working if it were false. T5: the man's range -- the Tyndall effect (a torch beam made visible by dust or milky water) and his 'optically pure air' experiments that helped kill spontaneous generation came from the same obsession with what a beam does when it meets stuff.
source: Grokipedia, 'John Tyndall' (1859 start; lampblacked copper-cube source, gas tube, thermopile + galvanometer; water vapour strongest absorber; CO2 and ozone significant; oxygen/nitrogen/hydrogen negligible; molecular-complexity pattern; Bakerian Lecture 12 December 1861; 'Contributions to Molecular Physics in the Domain of Radiant Heat', 1872). Wikipedia, 'Eunice Newton Foote' (two glass cylinders + air pump + four thermometers; air, CO2, hydrogen; 23 August 1856 AAAS Albany; read by Joseph Henry; American Journal of Science and Arts, September 1856; her quoted sentence; the scholarly caveat that her apparatus could not distinguish solar from terrestrial infrared). Wikipedia, 'Keeling Curve' (modern NDIR gas analysers descend from Tyndall's device).
framing_note: FIRM + CELEBRATED: this is the ladder that anchors the bank's declared position that greenhouse PHYSICS is real and settled, and it says so with no false balance backward. Voice = Victorian bench drama plus a modern checkable instrument. Dinner-test payoff = T1 (most of the air ignores Earth's heat entirely). Accuracy rails, all load-bearing: (1) water vapour IS the strongest absorber and the bank says so plainly -- that is Tyndall's result, not a talking point; (2) Tyndall did NOT discover the greenhouse effect -- Fourier proposed atmospheric heat retention in the 1820s and Tyndall found WHICH gases; a rung saying otherwise is an error; (3) Foote's 1856 priority is REAL but her sunlight setup could not isolate infrared -- state the difference honestly and never inflate it into a theft story; (4) any Tyndall quotation must be a verbatim sourced sentence or dropped entirely. Anti-restatement: never let a stem say 'gases that absorb infrared' before asking which gas surprised Tyndall -- describe the tube, the needle and the null result for dry air, and let the answer be recalled. Distractor mine = the real transparent gases (nitrogen, oxygen, hydrogen, argon), the real defeated heat theory (caloric), and real adjacent Victorians (Faraday, Fourier, Foote, Melloni, Pouillet).
history_overlap: science bank, physics/light strand: the Tyndall effect and 'why the sky is blue' may be built there -- this ladder keys the RADIANT-HEAT tube experiments and may touch the Tyndall effect only as a one-rung range note, never as a scattering explainer.

name: Arrhenius does it by hand -- and the forty-year exile
scope: The first calculated climate, the wrong number, and the objection that buried it. T2: in 1896 the Swedish chemist Svante Arrhenius, grinding through thousands of pen-and-paper calculations, published 'On the Influence of Carbonic Acid in the Air upon the Temperature of the Ground' in the Philosophical Magazine -- the first time anyone put a NUMBER on how much the ground would warm or cool if you changed the carbonic acid in the air. T2: his answers -- halving CO2 cools the ground about 4-5 degrees C; doubling it warms about 5-6 degrees C, with the biggest change at the poles. T3: what he was actually trying to explain was the ICE AGES, not industry -- he wanted to know what could plunge Europe under ice and then let it go. T3: where his carbon numbers came from -- the geologist Arvid Hogbom had worked out the natural carbon ledger (volcanoes in, rock weathering out) and noticed that the world's coal fires were already a comparable entry; Arrhenius put a temperature on Hogbom's bookkeeping. T3/T4: the honest misjudgment that makes this ladder unforgettable -- Arrhenius reckoned it would take roughly 3,000 years of coal burning to double CO2, and he WELCOMED the result: milder Swedish winters, better crops, an ice age postponed. The first man to compute greenhouse warming thought it would be pleasant. T4: the experiment that buried the idea -- in 1900 the Swedish physicist Knut Angstrom had CO2 absorption measured in a tube and reported that halving the CO2 changed the absorption by well under one percent; the band looked SATURATED, so extra CO2 could do nothing. It was an honest experiment, honestly accepted, and the CO2 theory went quiet for forty years. T4: the amateur who reopened it -- Guy Stewart Callendar, a British STEAM ENGINEER, hand-compiled world station temperature records and argued in a 1938 paper in the Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society that the world had warmed and rising CO2 was why; at the meeting the Society's Sir George Simpson said the agreement must be taken as a coincidence. T5: why Angstrom's saturation argument fails, and it is a beautiful mechanism a paragraph can carry -- the answer is ALTITUDE. Near the ground the band is saturated; high in the thin cold air it is not. Adding CO2 raises the HEIGHT from which Earth's heat finally escapes to space, and higher means colder means less radiated away. Gilbert Plass and others, using infrared spectroscopy improved by wartime work and the first electronic computers in the 1950s, made this quantitative and revived Arrhenius. T5: the modern scorecard, stated without flinching -- Arrhenius's 5-6 degrees for doubling ran hot; his own 1906 revision came down near 2 degrees, which sits inside the range scientists argue over today. The first NUMBER was wrong; the METHOD was right; both halves are the lesson.
source: Grokipedia, 'Svante Arrhenius' (1896 paper title and journal; halving -> 4-5 C cooling, doubling -> 5-6 C warming with polar amplification; thousands of manual calculations; Arvid Hogbom's 1894 carbon-cycle estimates; the ~3,000-year doubling estimate and his view that warming would be agriculturally beneficial; Knut Angstrom's 1900 saturation claim; the 1906 downward revision). Wikipedia, 'Guy Stewart Callendar' (steam engineer; 1938 'The artificial production of carbon dioxide and its influence on temperature', Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society; Sir George Simpson's 'coincidence' response; the 'Callendar effect'; Gilbert Plass's 1950s extension). Grokipedia, 'John Tyndall' (the absorption data Arrhenius built on).
framing_note: Voice = the bank's favourite shape, a right idea killed for forty years by a plausible experiment, plus the FIRM celebration of the physics. vision_mandated because it carries the 'greenhouse physics is settled' lean and because the Arrhenius-thought-it-was-nice fact cuts hard against lazy narratives in BOTH directions. Dinner-test payoff = the 'he hoped for it' rung. Accuracy rails: (1) NEVER present Arrhenius as prophesying catastrophe -- he predicted improvement and a slow 3,000-year timescale, and the ladder must say so; (2) Angstrom's saturation objection was real science honestly done and honestly believed, NOT suppression or fraud -- the fix is radiating altitude; a conspiracy framing here is a hard fail; (3) do not assert a precise calculation count ('10,000 calculations') unless the build sources it -- 'thousands of hand calculations' otherwise; (4) any Arrhenius quotation must be verbatim from a sourced edition of 'Worlds in the Making' (1908) or dropped. Anti-restatement: never let the stem explain saturation before asking why more CO2 still warms -- describe Angstrom's tube result and let 'the escape altitude rises into colder air' be recalled knowledge. Distractor mine = the ice-age causes that were genuinely live in 1896 (Croll's orbital theory, changing solar output, volcanic dust veils, continental uplift) and the real adjacent names (Hogbom, Angstrom, Chamberlin, Tyndall, Callendar, Plass). Lane border: MATH owns logarithms as a skill -- here the logarithmic relation is stated as a result, never drilled.
history_overlap: geography bank has a Milankovitch/ice-age T5 pair -- this ladder's ice-age framing must stay on Arrhenius's CO2 explanation and Croll must appear only as a distractor, never as the answer to an orbital-pacing question.

name: Keeling's stubborn curve
scope: Patient measurement as a monument. T1: since March 1958 one instrument high on the flank of Mauna Loa in Hawaii, sampling air that has crossed thousands of kilometres of open Pacific, has measured the carbon dioxide in the atmosphere without a break -- the longest unbroken record of a single number in the history of the air. The man who started it and never stopped: Charles David Keeling of the Scripps Institution of Oceanography. T1/T2: the shape everyone remembers is not a smooth climb, it SAWS -- up every northern winter, down every northern summer, about six parts per million each year. The cause is the Northern Hemisphere's forests and fields inhaling through the growing season and exhaling as leaves rot: Keeling's needle was recording the planet BREATHING. T2: the numbers -- roughly 315 parts per million when he began in 1958, well past 420 today, and anybody can check today's value because Scripps and NOAA publish it free. T3: the discovery that made a global record possible at all -- before Keeling, people assumed background CO2 varied wildly from place to place so a 'global' figure was meaningless. Testing his own homemade manometer at Big Sur and other sites, Keeling found that away from cities the AFTERNOON value was the same everywhere; the wild swings were local plants and traffic. Uniform background meant there was a real number worth measuring. T3: the obsession that makes the record trustworthy -- reference gas cylinders calibrated forward for decades, so that a reading taken this year is genuinely comparable to one taken in 1958. The monument is not a discovery; it is a REFUSAL TO STOP MEASURING. T4: the funding fights -- budget cuts in the mid-1960s killed his continuous South Pole record, and he scraped money together to keep Mauna Loa alive. The curve exists because one man would not let it die. T4: the obvious objection, met head on -- Mauna Loa is an ACTIVE VOLCANO that vents CO2. The protocol rejects data during downslope volcanic wind, exploits the regular day/night upslope-downslope air pattern, and is cross-checked against stations from Barrow in Alaska to the South Pole that trace the same curve. The objection was tested, not waved away. T5: what the curve settles and what it does not -- it settles that CO2 is rising, and by how much, better than almost any other quantity in earth science. It does not by itself settle how much warming follows, and the bank says both halves in the same breath. T5: how we know where the extra carbon came from -- the ratio of carbon-13 to carbon-12 in the air has been drifting in the direction expected from plant-derived (fossil) carbon, and atmospheric oxygen has been declining in step, as burning would require (the Suess effect).
source: Wikipedia, 'Keeling Curve' (Scripps; continuous Mauna Loa measurements from March 1958; 313 ppm March 1958 to 406 ppm November 2018 and rising ~2.5 ppm/yr; ~6 ppm seasonal cycle from land-vegetation uptake, May peak and September minimum; mid-1960s funding cuts ended the South Pole continuous record; earlier Big Sur test measurements and diurnal variation; infrared gas analysers). Scripps CO2 Program and NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory Mauna Loa record (current values, station protocol, calibration).
framing_note: Voice = the bank's monument to the scientific virtue that is not cleverness. Dinner-test payoff = the sawtooth (the planet breathes, and one needle recorded the breath). Accuracy rails: (1) give the 1958 figure as roughly 315 ppm and frame the CURRENT value as something the reader looks up rather than freezing a number that will go stale -- that framing is also the invitation; (2) the volcano objection must be stated as a serious objection with a real, specific answer, never sneered at; (3) no rung may let the rising curve stand in for a claim about how much warming follows -- the T5 'settles / does not settle' rung is mandatory; (4) the carbon-13 and oxygen-decline rung must be sourced precisely or dropped. Anti-restatement: never let a stem mention plants or seasons before asking what causes the sawtooth. Distractor mine = the real rival explanations for a seasonal wiggle (ocean solubility changing with temperature, volcanic venting, Southern Hemisphere seasons, instrument drift) and the real other observing stations (Barrow, Cape Grim, South Pole). Lane border: GEOGRAPHY owns Mauna Loa as a PLACE -- this ladder keys the measurement story only.
history_overlap: geography bank has a Darwin coral-reef rung set on the 'Keeling atoll' in the Indian Ocean -- a pure coincidence of names with no factual overlap, but no stem here may imply a connection, and the build should not use the word 'atoll' anywhere in this ladder.

name: Reading a climate nobody wrote down
scope: CONCEPT ladder: how do you take the temperature of a year no thermometer saw? Each rung is a different named method with its named case. T2: granite boulders sitting on limestone hundreds of kilometres from the nearest granite, and bedrock polished and scratched in long parallel grooves -- Louis Agassiz argued from these that a vanished ice sheet had once buried Europe. What he could NOT supply was a cause: he could show ice had been there and could not say why it came or why it left. T2/T3: the reversal that should be taught in every classroom -- William Buckland, Britain's foremost catastrophist, had read those same scratches as the work of Noah's Flood; he went into the field with Agassiz in 1840 and changed his mind IN PUBLIC. T3: tree rings -- the astronomer A. E. Douglass, hunting sunspot cycles in ring widths, invented crossdating, chaining the overlapping ring patterns of living trees back through dead beams, and ended up dating Southwestern pueblos to the exact year. T3/T4: ice cores, where the record stops being a proxy and becomes the thing itself -- the bubbles in a core are ACTUAL ancient atmosphere you can pump out and analyse; EPICA Dome C in Antarctica reached about 3,260 metres and 800,000 years, and the Vostok core, drilled to 3,623 metres by 1996, gave over 400,000 years and four earlier glacial cycles. T4: the isotope thermometer, one idea serving two archives -- water built with heavier oxygen-18 evaporates less readily and condenses sooner, so the ratio of oxygen-18 to oxygen-16 records the temperature at which the snow fell, and the SAME ratio in the shells of long-dead plankton in seafloor mud records the ocean. T4: the cross-check that makes cores comparable -- annual bands can be counted like tree rings (summer layers of large bubbles, winter layers of small), and a dated volcanic ash layer such as Tambora in 1815 or Laki in 1783 is a time stamp that lets two cores from opposite ends of Earth be lined up. T5: the order of events at the great thaws, which is the most abused fact in the whole argument -- through the deglaciations CO2 and temperature rise together, and ice records indicate CO2 lagged Antarctic warming by centuries at some terminations (Caillon and colleagues reported roughly 800 years, with substantial uncertainty; Parrenin and colleagues later found much closer synchrony at the most recent one). The mainstream reading is that an orbital nudge starts the thaw and CO2 amplifies it: there, CO2 is a feedback, not the trigger. The bank states this precisely and refuses BOTH cartoons. T5: the divergence problem -- since about 1960, tree rings at high northern latitudes have stopped tracking measured temperature the way they used to (Briffa and colleagues, 1998). A proxy that fails in the one stretch where we CAN check it is a warning about all the centuries where we cannot. T5: honest confidence as a NUMBER, not a mood -- the 2006 US National Research Council review graded its own certainty in tiers: high confidence for the last few centuries, less back to about AD 900, very little before that.
source: Wikipedia, 'Ice core' (trapped-bubble atmosphere sampling; oxygen-18/16 as a paleothermometer; annual layer counting with summer large-bubble and winter small-bubble layers; volcanic ash and dust markers; EPICA Dome C 3,260 m and 800,000 years). Wikipedia, 'Vostok Station' (3,623 m by 1996, usable climate data to 3,310 m and about 414,000 years, four previous glacial periods). Wikipedia, 'Medieval Warm Period' and 'Hockey stick graph (global temperature)' (Briffa et al. 1998 divergence problem; NRC/North 2006 confidence tiers). Caillon et al. 2003 (Science) and Parrenin et al. 2013 (Science) for the CO2 lag -- BUILD MUST READ BOTH DIRECTLY, not summaries.
framing_note: THEME ladder and the analytic backbone of the whole climate sub-strand: every stance rung downstream is worthless unless the kid first knows HOW anyone knows. Dinner-test payoff = the ice bubble (air from before there were farms, still sealed, waiting to be pumped out). Accuracy rails: (1) the CO2-lag rung is the single most misquoted fact in climate argument -- the build MUST source Caillon 2003 and Parrenin 2013 by name, must state the amplifier reading, must NOT overstate the lag, and must never let a distractor imply CO2 has no warming effect; (2) Agassiz had NO mechanism and the rung must say so -- his triumph and his gap are one rung each; (3) the NRC confidence tiers must be presented AS tiers, never flattened into 'scientists are confident'. Anti-restatement: describe what Buckland SAW in the field, not what he concluded. Distractor mine = the genuinely defeated rivals (Noah's Flood as the boulder-carrier; Lyell's drifting icebergs, which was a serious alternative; catastrophic uplift) and real rival proxies (corals, speleothems, boreholes, pollen, varves). Lane border, strictly enforced: GEOGRAPHY already owns the erratics tour and the 1837 Neuchatel scene -- this ladder keys the METHOD CHAIN and Buckland's public reversal.
history_overlap: geography bank, confirmed live rungs: Agassiz's 1837 Neuchatel claim answered as 'immense sheets of ice' with 'a great biblical Flood' as the rival, plus the Big Rock/Okotoks erratic, the Foothills Erratics Train, the Madison Boulder, the Norber perched blocks, Lake Agassiz and the Younger Dryas, and a Dome C ice-core Milankovitch rung. NONE of those facts may be re-keyed here; this ladder keys Buckland's conversion, crossdating, the trapped-bubble idea, the oxygen-isotope thermometer, layer counting and ash time stamps, the CO2-lag order, the divergence problem and the NRC confidence tiers.

name: Milankovic's thirty years of arithmetic
scope: A prisoner of war, a library desk, and the clockwork of the ice ages. T2: in 1914 a Serbian civil engineer had his honeymoon interrupted by the assassination in Sarajevo, was arrested by Austro-Hungarian authorities as an enemy reserve officer and shipped to an internment camp at Nezsider. Within months his old Vienna professor's connections got him released to Budapest, where Kalman Szily, director of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences library, gave him a desk and let him work undisturbed -- under orders not to leave the city and to report weekly to the police. Milutin Milankovic spent the war computing how much sunlight had fallen on each latitude of Earth in the deep past. T3: what he computed, by hand -- insolation tables spanning about 600,000 years, latitude by latitude, one arithmetic line at a time, work that filled decades and that a laptop now redoes in a fraction of a second. T3: the three wobbles -- the orbit's shape stretches and relaxes over roughly 100,000 years; the axis tips between about 22.1 and 24.5 degrees over about 41,000 years; and the axis's slow gyroscope wobble shifts WHICH season falls at Earth's closest approach to the Sun over about 19,000 to 23,000 years. T4: his key insight was not 'colder' but WHERE and WHEN -- an ice age begins when northern summers are too cool to melt the previous winter's snow. Snow that survives one summer reflects sunlight and helps make the next summer cooler still. Winter snowfall is not the lever; summer melting is. T4: the man he shared the idea with and eclipsed -- the self-taught Scot James Croll had argued for orbital control of the ice ages in the 1860s and 1870s and was largely forgotten; Milankovic's contribution was to make it CALCULABLE for a given latitude and epoch. T4/T5: the manuscript went to the printer on 2 April 1941. Four days later Belgrade was bombed and the printing house destroyed -- but the printed sheets survived almost undamaged in the warehouse, and the 626-page 'Canon of Insolation and the Ice-Age Problem' appeared that year anyway. T5: the vindication he did not live to see -- in 1976 Hays, Imbrie and Shackleton found the roughly 100,000-, 41,000- and 23,000-year beats written into oxygen-isotope records from deep-sea sediment cores; their paper was titled 'Variations in the Earth's Orbit: Pacemaker of the Ice Ages'. Milankovic had died in 1958. T5 (MYSTERY rung): the hole still in the theory -- for the last million years the strongest beat in the record is the roughly 100,000-year one, but that orbital cycle changes the total sunlight Earth receives by only a tiny amount. Why the weakest push produces the biggest response is called the 100,000-year problem, and nobody has settled it.
source: Grokipedia, 'Milutin Milankovic' (POW internment during WWI; hand-computed insolation tables over ~600,000 years; the 1920 'Theorie mathematique...'; 1930 'Mathematische Klimalehre'; the 1941 'Kanon der Erdbestrahlung'; the three cycles with their periods and the 22.1-24.5 degree obliquity range; northern-summer-insolation control of ice-sheet growth; deep-sea oxygen-isotope confirmation). Wikipedia, 'Milutin Milankovic' (arrest in 1914, camp at Nezsider, release 24 December 1914, Kalman Szily and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences library, weekly police reporting; manuscript sent to press 2 April 1941, printing house destroyed in the 6 April 1941 bombing of Belgrade with the printed sheets surviving in the warehouse; 626 pages; James Croll's earlier and forgotten orbital theory). Hays, Imbrie and Shackleton 1976, Science -- BUILD MUST VERIFY the citation and wording directly.
framing_note: Discovery ladder with a genuine MYSTERY ceiling -- the shape the bank loves: an obsessive computation, a long wait, a vindication, and an honest unsolved remainder. Dinner-test payoff = the prisoner given a library desk. Accuracy rails: (1) he was moved OUT of the internment camp to Budapest under reporting restrictions -- do NOT write that he did the work in a prison cell; (2) the printing house was destroyed in the GERMAN bombing of Belgrade on 6 April 1941 and the printed sheets SURVIVED -- any source saying Allied bombing is wrong for that date; (3) the 100,000-year problem must be presented as genuinely open, with no distractor secretly being the answer. Anti-restatement: put the SCENE (a POW with a desk, a war on, tables of numbers) in the stem and let the man, the cycle or the vindication be recalled. Distractor mine = the ice-age causes that were real rivals (Arrhenius's CO2, changing solar output, volcanic dust veils, continental drift and uplift, Croll's version) and the other two orbital cycles as wrong options against the right one. Lane border: geography's earth-system backbone already tours the ice-core rhythm and states the eccentricity puzzle -- this ladder keys the MAN, the hand arithmetic, the summer-melt insight, Croll's priority and the 1976 marine-core vindication.
history_overlap: geography bank, two confirmed T5 rungs: the Dome C ice core's ~100,000-year rhythm answered as 'the Milankovitch cycles', and the puzzle that eccentricity 'barely changes how much sunlight Earth receives'. This ladder must NEVER ask 'what are the cycles called?' and must key the 100,000-year problem only as Milankovic's unfinished business, framed through the 1976 marine-core vindication rather than through ice cores.

name: Warm Vikings, frozen Thames: the climate before the smokestacks
scope: Large natural swings, on the record, before industry. T1: around 985 Erik the Red led settlers from Iceland to southwest Greenland, and for roughly four centuries Norse farmers there kept cattle, sheep and goats and built stone churches on ground that later froze hard -- European farms in GREENLAND. The last surviving document from the settlements is dated 1412, and then they are gone. T2: why the colony's end is NOT a tidy climate parable -- Greenland's export was walrus ivory, and the market collapsed when African elephant ivory reached Europe; isotope work on Norse bones shows the diet shifting heavily to seal. Cooling was a real pressure; trade collapse, soil erosion and human choices were pressures too, and the bank names all of them. T2/T3: how we know it was warm -- Greenland and Icelandic ice cores, the Icelandic annals and sagas, and dated Norse building sites now sitting in permafrost. T3: the swing the other way, from roughly 1300 to 1850 -- Alpine glaciers advanced onto farmland and over hamlets, Dutch painters filled canvases with frozen canals, and in London the Thames froze at the city in 24 recorded winters between 1400 and 1831. T3/T4: single cold years that can be traced to a CAUSE -- the Laki eruption in Iceland in 1783 and Tambora in 1815, whose ash and sulphate gave 1816 its name as 'the year without a summer' in New England and Europe, and left a dated layer in ice cores at both poles. T4: the blank Sun -- from about 1645 to 1715 astronomers with the newly invented telescope recorded almost no sunspots; in the 28 years from 1672 to 1699 fewer than 50 were logged, against the tens of thousands an equivalent modern span would record. Gustav Sporer found the gap in the 1880s, E. W. Maunder wrote it up in 1890 and 1894, and it lay forgotten until John A. Eddy revived it in a 1976 Science paper and gave it the name we use. T4/T5: the honest caveat, which the bank supplies itself -- the Maunder Minimum sits INSIDE the Little Ice Age but the cooling began before it, and the leading explanation for the coldest stretches is volcanic. The bank does not swap one tidy story for another. T5: the contested part, framed as contested -- was the Medieval Warm Period global? The North Atlantic evidence is strong, but the PAGES 2k synthesis found that peak warmth did NOT occur at the same time in different regions, and the IPCC's position has been that the evidence does not support globally synchronous medieval warmth exceeding recent decades. The durable lesson the bank does assert: the climate swung hard, repeatedly, long before any smokestack. T5: what the swings cost -- famine years and harvest failures across the Little Ice Age, from the 1690s Scottish 'ill years' to the Irish famine of 1740-41. Climate has been shoving human history around for as long as there has been human history.
source: Wikipedia, 'Medieval Warm Period' (about 950-1250 CE; strongest in western Europe, Iceland and Greenland; Norse settlements founded around 985; last document 1412; economic drivers of abandonment; PAGES 2k 2019 finding of non-synchrony; IPCC Third Assessment wording; global comparison to 20th-century means). Wikipedia, 'Maunder Minimum' (about 1645-1715; fewer than 50 sunspots recorded 1672-1699 against 40,000-50,000 in a modern equivalent; Sporer 1887 and 1889; Maunder 1890 and 1894; Eddy's 1976 Science paper; cooling beginning before the solar minimum with volcanic activity as the leading cause; severe winters 1683-84, 1694-95, 1708-09). Wikipedia, 'River Thames frost fairs' (24 recorded freezes at London 1400-1831; last fair 1-4 February 1814). Wikipedia, 'Ice core' (Tambora and Laki as dated ash markers).
framing_note: CORE STANCE LADDER, vision_mandated. The bank's declared lean -- the geological and historical record makes large climate swings the NORM, before any industrial CO2 -- is stated plainly and shown with dated evidence. The discipline is symmetric and non-negotiable: the same ladder must refuse to convert 'it swung before' into 'therefore CO2 does nothing', and must refuse to convert the Maunder Minimum into a tidy solar explanation the evidence does not support. PRESENT, never preach; no gloating rung. Dinner-test payoff = T1, European farms on Greenland. Accuracy rails: (1) the Norse collapse is MULTI-CAUSAL and the ladder must say so -- climate plus the ivory-trade collapse plus erosion; a single-cause morality tale is a hard fail; (2) the Maunder Minimum did not cause the Little Ice Age on its own -- the cooling started earlier and volcanic forcing leads current explanations, and that rung is mandatory; (3) the global-synchrony question is DISPUTED and must be framed as disputed, naming PAGES 2k; the bank must NOT assert the MWP was globally warmer than today. Anti-restatement: give the SCENE (a stone church in Greenland, an advancing glacier, a telescope logbook with nothing in it) and let the answer be recalled. Distractor mine = the real rival explanations for the Little Ice Age (volcanic sulphate, ocean-circulation change, orbital drift, sea-ice feedbacks) and the real other solar minima (Sporer, Wolf, Dalton).
history_overlap: geography bank, BANNED facts (already live there): the 1814 Thames frost fair with the elephant led across the ice; the Old London Bridge nineteen-pier explanation for the freezing; and the Little Ice Age Stradivari dense-spruce violin-wood theory. This ladder may state the '24 freezes 1400-1831' count but must not re-key any of those three. history bank: Erik the Red and the Norse voyages are a probable Viking-episode ladder there -- this ladder keys the CLIMATE evidence, the dated 1412 endpoint and the multi-causal collapse, not the saga.

name: The hockey stick fight
scope: What happens to a graph when it becomes a logo, and what an audit is for. T3: in 1998 and 1999 Michael Mann, Raymond Bradley and Malcolm Hughes published Northern Hemisphere temperature reconstructions -- in Nature back to 1400, then in Geophysical Research Letters back to 1000 -- combining tree rings, corals, ice cores and documentary records into one curve: a long gentle decline, then a sharp 20th-century rise. The shape gave it its nickname. T3: the graph's political life -- the IPCC's 2001 Third Assessment Report put it in the Summary for Policymakers and blew it up as a poster-sized backdrop for the televised launch. A research figure became an emblem, and emblems are hard to revise. T4: the audit -- Stephen McIntyre, a Canadian mineral-exploration statistician, and the economist Ross McKitrick could not reproduce the result from the published description, so they asked for the data and the code. Their 2003 and 2005 papers argued that the principal-component step had been centred on the 20th century rather than on the whole record, which pushed hockey-stick-shaped series into the leading component, and that the shape leaned heavily on a small set of bristlecone-pine records. T4: what the referee actually said -- the 2006 US National Research Council panel agreed the centring convention had a bias and was 'not recommended', separately advised that strip-bark bristlecone-pine records be avoided in temperature reconstructions, and concluded that the broad recent-warmth picture survived when other methods were used. It also graded its own confidence in tiers: high for the last four centuries, less back to AD 900, very little before. T5: the problem underneath the fight -- Keith Briffa's 1998 Nature paper had shown that since about 1960 northern tree rings stopped tracking measured warming. Why does the thermometer of the past fail in the one period we can test it against real thermometers? Still not fully answered. T5: Climategate -- in November 2009 emails taken from the Climatic Research Unit at the University of East Anglia were published, including Phil Jones writing that he had used 'Mike's Nature trick' to 'hide the decline'. What that actually did: on a 1999 World Meteorological Organization cover graphic, post-1960 tree-ring values were replaced with instrumental temperatures, so a reader saw one continuous line and could not see the proxy failing. 'Trick' is ordinary scientist-slang for a technique -- and the splice was not explained on the graphic. T5: the verdict, both halves reported -- eight inquiries found no fraud or scientific misconduct and did not doubt the scientists' honesty, and the Muir Russell review nonetheless judged that 1999 figure MISLEADING, though not deliberately so. The bank reports both sentences and lets them stand together. T5: what the fight really settled -- that a published result must arrive with data and code a stranger can rerun. Routine public archiving of reconstruction data and code became normal AFTER the audits. Replication as a right, not a favour.
source: Wikipedia, 'Hockey stick graph (global temperature)' (MBH98 in Nature 23 April 1998 back to 1400; MBH99 in Geophysical Research Letters March 1999 back to 1000; IPCC TAR 2001 Summary for Policymakers and the poster backdrop at Sir John Houghton's launch; McIntyre and McKitrick 2003 and 2005 on the 1902-1980 centring period and the resulting component selection; the 2006 NRC/North panel's finding that the contested PCA had a small bias and was not recommended but had little influence, and its confidence statement about the last four centuries; the Briffa 1998 divergence problem). Wikipedia, 'Climatic Research Unit email controversy' (November 2009 release from the University of East Anglia; 'Mike's Nature trick' and 'hide the decline'; the 1999 WMO cover illustration; the Muir Russell review finding the graph misleading though not deliberately so; eight committees finding no fraud). NRC 2006, 'Surface Temperature Reconstructions for the Last 2,000 Years' -- BUILD MUST READ the strip-bark recommendation and the confidence tiers directly.
framing_note: vision_mandated and the hardest ladder in the sub-strand to keep honest. The bank does NOT declare the hockey stick fake and does NOT declare the critics debunked; it reports the specific findings of the specific referee -- the centring was biased and not recommended, strip-bark bristlecones should be avoided, the broad recent-warmth conclusion survived other methods, and confidence collapses before AD 900 -- and it reports both Climategate sentences: no fraud found, AND the WMO figure judged misleading. No sneering at Mann; no hagiography of McIntyre. Dinner-test payoff = 'hide the decline' explained CORRECTLY, because a kid who can explain what the splice actually did understands more than either shouting side. Accuracy rails: (1) never state or imply that Mann was found guilty of fraud -- he was not; (2) never state that the critics were simply wrong -- the NRC endorsed part of their statistical point; (3) quote the NRC confidence as TIERS; (4) the 'trick' rung must give both the ordinary-slang meaning and what the splice concealed, in the same rung. Distractor mine = real proxies (corals, boreholes, speleothems, varves, pollen) and the real people involved (Briffa, Jones, Wahl, Ammann, von Storch, Wegman) -- never joke options. Lane border: PHILOSOPHY owns 'what makes a claim scientific' as a seminar question; here falsification is WORKING PRACTICE -- can a stranger rerun your code?
history_overlap: science bank, howscience strand: the replication-crisis, Ioannidis and 'peer review is not a truth-detector' ladders will make the general case -- this ladder must key ONLY the climate-reconstruction specifics (short-centred PCA, bristlecone strip-bark, the divergence problem, the WMO splice, the archiving change) and must not restate the general 'peer review missed X' fact. This sub-strand's 'Reading a climate nobody wrote down' ladder introduces the divergence problem and the NRC tiers -- coordinate so each appears as a rung in only ONE of the two ladders.

name: Prophecies with dates on them
scope: CONCEPT ladder: the falsifiable forecast, and what the scoreboard says -- every rung a named forecaster, a dated forecast, and the outcome. T2: Paul Ehrlich opened 'The Population Bomb' in 1968 with the line that the battle to feed all of humanity was over and that in the 1970s hundreds of millions of people would starve to death. What happened instead was Norman Borlaug's dwarf wheat and India's Green Revolution: India roughly tripled its population and became broadly self-sufficient in food, and per-capita calories rose worldwide. T3: the wager -- in 1980 the economist Julian Simon bet Ehrlich that any raw materials Ehrlich chose would be CHEAPER in ten years. Ehrlich and colleagues picked chromium, copper, nickel, tin and tungsten, 200 dollars of each. In October 1990 Ehrlich mailed Simon a cheque for 576 dollars and 7 cents. An argument settled by a number on a date. T3/T4: the ice-free Arctic deadlines -- in December 2007 a BBC report carried Wieslaw Maslowski's projection that the Arctic could be ice-free in summer as early as 2013; Peter Wadhams later named 2015-2016. The Arctic still has summer sea ice. AND, in the same breath, the bank states the other half: satellite records began in 1979, September extent has fallen sharply since, and the record minimum of about 3.41 million square kilometres was set on 2 September 2012. The DEADLINE failed; the trend did not. T4: the drowned Maldives -- in 1988 news reports carried a Maldivian official's warning that the islands could be completely covered within 30 years; 2018 came and went. Meanwhile aerial and satellite studies of Pacific and Indian Ocean reef islands (Kench and colleagues) found most atoll islands stable or GROWING in area, because coral rubble and sand accrete faster than the sea rises. The honest other half: island AREA is not the same as habitability, and the Maldives is spending heavily on defences. T4: the bank turns the same knife on its own side -- in the 1970s magazines ran a coming-ice-age scare, most famously Newsweek's 'The Cooling World' in 1975. When Thomas Peterson, William Connolley and John Fleck surveyed the peer-reviewed literature of 1965-1979 for the Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society in 2008, they found papers predicting WARMING far outnumbered papers predicting cooling. The 'they predicted an ice age' talking point is itself overstated, and this ladder says so. T5: the anatomy of a failed forecast -- the 1968 projections assumed food output would keep growing the way it had; they did not model Borlaug. Models fail when the thing that changes is the thing they held fixed. T5: criticism from INSIDE the field -- a 2022 Nature comment by Zeke Hausfather and colleagues, 'Climate simulations: recognize the hot model problem', warned that some of the newest models produce warming higher than other lines of evidence support and urged researchers to stop treating all model output as equally credible. Published in Nature, by people who accept human-caused warming. T5: what a prediction is FOR -- a forecast with a date on it is a gift, because it can be graded. A forecast without one cannot be wrong, and a claim that cannot be wrong is not yet science.
source: Wikipedia, 'The Population Bomb' (1968, Ballantine/Sierra Club; the opening lines about the battle to feed humanity and hundreds of millions starving in the 1970s; the India predictions; the Green Revolution outcome and the Ehrlichs' later concession that their timing was 'way off'). Wikipedia, 'Simon-Ehrlich wager' (29 September 1980 to 29 September 1990; chromium, copper, nickel, tin and tungsten chosen by Ehrlich and colleagues; 200 dollars of each; all five cheaper in real terms; cheque for 576.07 dollars mailed October 1990). Wikipedia, 'Global cooling' (Newsweek 'The Cooling World' 1975; the 1975 NAS report's own caveat; Peterson, Connolley and Fleck 2008 finding warming dominated the 1965-1979 literature). Wikipedia, 'Arctic sea ice decline' (satellite record from 1979; record minimum 3.41 million km2 on 2 September 2012; ~4.7% per decade September decline). BUILD MUST SOURCE DIRECTLY, none of these could be fetched here: the BBC News report of December 2007 carrying Maslowski's projection; Wadhams's dated statements; Al Gore's December 2009 Copenhagen remark and its exact attribution; the 1988 Maldives report; Kench and colleagues' atoll-island area studies; Hausfather et al. 2022 in Nature; and the exact Peterson 2008 paper counts.
framing_note: vision_mandated -- the bank's FAILED-PREDICTIONS lean, executed with maximum discipline. Every rung names the person, the date and the outcome; there are no anonymous 'they said' rungs and no strawmen. Dinner-test payoff = the 576-dollar cheque. Accuracy rails, all load-bearing: (1) a failed DEADLINE must NEVER be presented as disproving a trend -- the Arctic rung must state in the same rung that summer sea ice has declined substantially since 1979, and a build that omits this fails the ladder; (2) every quoted forecast must be verbatim with its year and forecaster, or dropped -- if the build cannot source Maslowski's or Gore's exact wording, cut that rung rather than paraphrase; (3) the 1970s cooling rung is MANDATORY and lands against the bank's own side -- it is the Feynman rung ('you must not fool yourself, and you are the easiest person to fool') and the reason the rest of the ladder can be trusted; (4) the Maldives rung must carry the habitability caveat. Tone rail: the documented record is damning enough -- NO gloating, no 'so much for the experts' voice, no contempt for the forecasters as people. Distractor mine = real named forecasters and real outcomes (Borlaug, Simon, Ehrlich, Maslowski, Wadhams, the Club of Rome's 'Limits to Growth', the 1975 NAS report) -- never joke options. Lane borders: ECONOMICS owns the Simon-Ehrlich bet as a price-signal and resource-scarcity lesson; here it is keyed as a DATED, GRADED PREDICTION. PHILOSOPHY owns Popper on falsifiability as theory; here falsifiability is the working habit of putting a date on your claim.
history_overlap: economics bank: the Simon-Ehrlich wager, Borlaug and the Green Revolution are natural economics/history topics -- flag for cross-bank dedup; this ladder keys them strictly as dated predictions and their outcomes. science bank, howscience strand: if a general 'expert forecasting record' or Ehrlich/WEF ladder is built there, the Simon-Ehrlich bet must live in exactly one of the two, not both.

name: What 'ninety-seven percent' counted
scope: A counting lesson dressed as a slogan. T3: the number everyone has heard -- in 2013 John Cook and colleagues published a study in Environmental Research Letters that read 11,944 paper abstracts published between 1991 and 2011 and reported that 97.1 percent endorsed the consensus on human-caused warming. The fact the slogan leaves out: 66.4 percent of those abstracts expressed NO POSITION at all and were set aside before the percentage was taken. The 97 percent is a percentage of the remaining third. T3/T4: what 'endorse' was defined to mean -- the study's largest endorsement category was IMPLICIT: a paper counted if it simply took human contribution for granted without saying how much. A paper saying humans contribute and a paper saying humans are the dominant cause both landed inside the same 97 percent, and only a small fraction explicitly quantified human causation as more than half. T4: the OTHER 97 percent, because there are two -- Doran and Zimmerman's 2009 survey emailed 10,257 earth scientists and received 3,146 replies, then narrowed to 79 respondents who were climate specialists publishing mostly on climate; of those, nearly all agreed temperatures had risen and that human activity was a significant factor. The famous figure rests on a subgroup of 79 people. T4: the published pushback that is hardest to dismiss -- Richard Tol, an economist and IPCC contributing author who ACCEPTS human-caused warming, published a critique arguing the abstract-rating procedure lacked controls and any measurement of rater reliability. Criticism from someone on the same side of the physics is the strongest kind. T5: what is broadly agreed and what genuinely is not, stated as two lists -- not in serious dispute: CO2 absorbs infrared (Tyndall, re-measured by commercial instruments daily), atmospheric CO2 has risen (Keeling, checkable today), and the world has warmed since the 19th century (confirmed by a skeptic-led re-analysis). Genuinely disputed among publishing scientists: the size of climate sensitivity, the attribution of individual extreme events, and the economic damage estimate. The consensus is broad on the first list and much narrower on the second. T5: the deeper move -- a head count is a fact about SCIENTISTS; evidence is a fact about the WORLD. Semmelweis, Wegener and Marshall were each on the losing side of a head count, and each was right.
source: Wikipedia, 'Surveys of scientists' views on climate change' (Cook et al. 2013: 11,944 abstracts from 1991-2011; 66.4 percent expressing no position; 97.1 percent of those expressing a position endorsing the consensus; author self-ratings of 35.5 percent no position and 97.2 percent of the remainder; Doran and Zimmerman 2009: 10,257 polled, 3,146 responses, the 79-climatologist subgroup, 76 of 79 on rising temperatures and 75 on human activity as significant; Richard Tol's methodological critique on controls and rater reliability). BUILD MUST READ Cook et al. 2013 in Environmental Research Letters DIRECTLY for the endorsement-level definitions and the count of papers explicitly quantifying human causation, and must verify the Doran subgroup denominators before writing any rung on them.
framing_note: vision_mandated -- the bank's methodological critique of the 97 percent claim, delivered as ARITHMETIC and never as attitude. The whole ladder is one question asked five ways: what was in the denominator? Dinner-test payoff = the 66.4 percent who said nothing being removed before the percentage was computed. Accuracy rails: (1) the bank does NOT say the figure is a lie or that scientists secretly disagree about the greenhouse effect -- it says the number conflates 'humans contribute' with 'humans are the primary driver and catastrophe follows', and the T5 rung stating the FIRM list loudly is mandatory, not optional balance; (2) the Cook numbers must be exact -- 11,944, 66.4 percent, 97.1 percent -- and the endorsement-level description must come from the paper itself, not from a summary; (3) Tol must be identified as someone who accepts human-caused warming, or the rung reads as team sport; (4) the word 'denier' is BANNED everywhere in this ladder, including in distractors and context. Anti-restatement: never let a stem mention 'papers with no position' before asking what the 97 percent was a percentage OF. Distractor mine = the other real survey numbers and their authors (Oreskes 2004's 928 abstracts, Doran's 79, Anderegg, Verheggen) and real named critics -- never joke options. Lane border: MATH owns percentage arithmetic as a drill; here the arithmetic IS the wonder.

name: What the thermometers actually say
scope: The messiest dataset in science, audited in public. T3: the problem nobody thinks about -- a thermometer that read faithfully for 120 years is still a problem if the town grew around it, or if the hour of reading changed. Around 1900 most American volunteer observers read their maximum-minimum thermometers in the late afternoon; over the century most switched to morning, and reading at a different hour double-counts hot or cold days. The raw record therefore has a step in it that has nothing to do with climate. This time-of-observation bias is documented and correcting it is legitimate -- the bank concedes the strongest point against its own instinct FIRST. T3: the urban heat island, and a test a kid can run -- brick, asphalt and concrete store the day's sun and release it after dark, so a city centre can run several degrees warmer than open country on a calm clear night. Luke Howard measured London's centre at about 2.1 degrees C warmer than the surrounding countryside at night in the 1810s. Anyone with a car thermometer and a drive out of town after sunset can reproduce it. T4: the audit -- Anthony Watts's volunteer surfacestations project photographed United States Historical Climatology Network sites one by one and reported that a large share sat beside air-conditioner exhausts, parking lots, runways and buildings, in breach of the network's own siting rules. T4: what was BUILT instead of argued -- rather than keep fighting, NOAA commissioned the US Climate Reference Network: deliberately pristine rural sites, triple-redundant temperature sensors, commissioned in 2004 and reaching 114 stations across the contiguous states by 2008, designed so that no adjustment would be needed at all. Building a new instrument to settle a dispute is the most scientific act in this ladder. T4/T5: the skeptic who ran his own numbers and published the answer that went against him -- Richard Muller, publicly doubtful of the surface record, founded Berkeley Earth in 2010 with funding that included the Charles G. Koch Foundation, and set out to test the three specific skeptic objections: station siting, urban heat island, and data-selection bias. After analysing over 1.6 billion readings from about 39,000 stations, his group reported land warming of about 0.91 degrees C over fifty years, essentially confirming the existing records, and in a July 2012 New York Times piece Muller wrote that he had gone further still and now thought humans were almost entirely the cause. T5: the sea, which is most of the record -- before about 1940 most ocean temperatures came from hauling up a canvas bucket, which cools by evaporation on the way to the deck; afterwards most came from engine-room intakes, which run warm. That transition put a step into the global record, and how large a correction it needs is still argued. T5: the honest scoreboard -- adjustments are published, documented and reversible; over the US LAND record they INCREASE the trend; over the global OCEAN record they REDUCE the century-scale trend; and neither the pristine new network nor the skeptic-led re-analysis overturned the warming. The bank refuses 'the data is faked' and refuses 'the data needs no scrutiny'.
source: Wikipedia, 'Berkeley Earth' (founded 2010 by Richard and Elizabeth Muller; Muller's own 2012 statement that he had identified problems throwing doubt on the very existence of global warming; funders including Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, the Charles G. Koch Foundation, FICER and the Bowes Foundation with no donor control; the three skeptic concerns tested; over 1.6 billion measurements from about 39,000 stations; 0.91 +/- 0.05 C land warming over fifty years; the July 2012 New York Times op-ed and 'humans are almost entirely the cause'). Wikipedia, 'U.S. Climate Reference Network' (prototype 2000, commissioned January 2004, 114 contiguous-US stations by 2008 and 137 total by 2023; pristine representative siting expected to remain undeveloped; multi-sensor instrumentation; 2016 research showing USHCN adjustments moved its trends toward nearby USCRN stations). Wikipedia, 'Urban heat island' (typical day and night magnitudes; thermal mass, albedo, reduced evapotranspiration and urban-canyon geometry; Luke Howard's 1810s London measurement of about 2.1 C at night). BUILD MUST SOURCE DIRECTLY: the surfacestations 2009 report's exact percentages, NOAA's time-of-observation-bias documentation, and the bucket-to-intake sea-surface adjustment literature.
framing_note: vision_mandated -- the bank's 'adjustments and urban heat island named' lean, delivered as a FAIR FIGHT that the skeptics partly won (the siting really was bad, and the USCRN exists because of it) and partly lost (the warming survived the audit). Dinner-test payoff = Muller publishing the result that went against him -- that rung is the moral centre of the whole sub-strand and the bank's own virtue in action. Accuracy rails: (1) the ladder must NOT leave a kid believing the temperature record is fabricated -- the Berkeley Earth and USCRN rungs are mandatory and may not be softened or cut for length; (2) equally it must not leave a kid believing the record needs no scrutiny -- the time-of-observation, siting and bucket-versus-intake rungs are mandatory; (3) the surfacestations percentages and the Berkeley Earth figures must be sourced exactly and never rounded up for effect; (4) name the funding plainly -- Koch money paid for a study whose result the funders did not want -- with no insinuation in either direction. Anti-restatement: describe the SITE (a thermometer beside an air-conditioner exhaust; a pristine field with three sensors) and let the named project or person be recalled. Distractor mine = the real competing datasets and their owners (NASA GISS, NOAA GHCN, HadCRUT, JMA, ERA5, UAH, RSS) and the real named adjustment problems (time of observation, station moves, the liquid-in-glass to MMTS instrument change, bucket-to-intake). Test-it-yourself invitation lives at T3: the drive out of town after sunset.

name: The greening nobody forecast
scope: A measured, inconvenient, cheerful fact -- and the same standard applied to it. T3: since 1982 two satellite instruments, NOAA's Advanced Very High Resolution Radiometer and NASA's Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer, have measured how much leaf a patch of ground carries. A 2016 study in Nature Climate Change led by Zaichun Zhu reported that between a quarter and a half of Earth's vegetated land had greened significantly over 35 years -- extra leaf area equivalent to about TWICE the area of the continental United States. The satellites were not looking for good news; they were counting leaves. T3/T4: the mechanism, which is ordinary plant physiology -- CO2 is a plant's raw material, and in richer air a leaf's stomata can open less to take in the same carbon, so the plant loses less water for the same growth. That is why the greening shows up most strongly at dry margins (teach 'stomata' and 'water-use efficiency' before testing them). T4: the attribution and its honest limit -- the study's models attributed roughly 70 percent of the greening to CO2 fertilization and about 9 percent to nitrogen deposition. The leaf-area increase is an OBSERVATION; the 70 percent is a MODEL output. The bank draws that line here, on a fact it likes, because that is the same line it demands elsewhere. T4: the direct test rather than the model -- FACE experiments (Free-Air CO2 Enrichment) ring real forest and cropland with pipes and fumigate them with elevated CO2 for years, measuring what actually grows. The results were generally smaller than sealed-greenhouse studies had promised, and were limited wherever nitrogen or water ran short. T4/T5: the other half the bank must tell -- a 2019 study in Nature Sustainability led by Chi Chen found China and India alone accounted for about a third of the new green, much of it from tree-planting programmes and intensive cropping, that is, land MANAGEMENT rather than CO2; and crops grown under elevated CO2 have been measured with lower concentrations of protein, zinc and iron. More leaf is not automatically more nutrition. T5: what greening does and does not license -- extra plant growth pulls CO2 back out of the air (the land carbon sink), which is a real negative feedback already counted in carbon budgets. It is not a cancellation of warming, and the rung refuses the cartoon in both directions.
source: NASA release on Zhu et al. 2016, 'Carbon Dioxide Fertilization Greening Earth, Study Finds' (a quarter to a half of Earth's vegetated land significantly greened over 1982-2015; roughly 70 percent attributed to CO2 fertilization and 9 percent to nitrogen; MODIS and AVHRR leaf area index; extra foliage equivalent to twice the continental United States; the team's caveats about acclimation and about attribution depending on models). BUILD MUST SOURCE DIRECTLY: Zhu et al. 2016 in Nature Climate Change itself; Chen et al. 2019 in Nature Sustainability for the China/India share; the FACE experiment yield literature; and Myers et al. 2014 in Nature for the crop protein, zinc and iron findings.
framing_note: vision_mandated -- the bank's 'CO2 greening is real' lean, deliberately sourced to NASA's own release so the reader can check it at a source no one will call fringe. Dinner-test payoff = extra leaves equal to twice the continental United States. Accuracy rails: (1) greening must NOT be allowed to become an argument that warming is harmless -- the T5 limits rung is mandatory; (2) the observation/attribution line must stay bright: the leaf-area increase is measured and the 70 percent CO2 share is modelled, and the ladder must say so -- applying the bank's own standard to a fact the bank LIKES is the point of this ladder existing; (3) the nutrient-dilution and land-management findings are mandatory, not decorative balance; (4) no figure may be used unless the build has read the study, not a press summary. Anti-restatement: the stem gives the satellite measurement and the surprise; the answer is the driver or the mechanism, recalled. Distractor mine = the real rival explanations for greening, all partly true and therefore excellent live options (longer growing seasons from warming, nitrogen deposition, irrigation and land-use change, regrowth on abandoned farmland). Lane borders: ANIMAL owns creatures that eat plants; COOKING owns crops as food; here the anchor is the SATELLITE MEASUREMENT and the leaf.
history_overlap: geography bank may carry a Sahel-greening or Great Green Wall place-anchored rung -- flag for a cross-bank check; this ladder keys the GLOBAL satellite leaf-area measurement and its attribution, never a single place.

name: Koonin reads the report himself
scope: The mature view, and a method a reader can copy with a library card. T3: the credential that makes this ladder work -- Steven Koonin was a Caltech theoretical physicist from 1975, the institute's provost from 1995 to 2004, chief scientist at BP, and President Obama's Under Secretary for Science at the Department of Energy from May 2009 to November 2011, reporting to the Nobel laureate Steven Chu and running a science budget of over five billion dollars a year across ten national laboratories. He is not an outsider throwing stones. T3/T4: the METHOD, which is the point of the whole ladder -- in his 2021 book 'Unsettled' Koonin did not build a rival climate model. He READ the IPCC assessment reports and the US National Climate Assessment themselves, and set what their technical chapters actually say beside what the press releases and headlines say they say. The tool is a library card, and the reports are free online. T4: a worked example -- the assessment reports' own text reports low confidence in long-term trends in tropical cyclone activity, while coverage built on top of them routinely asserts hurricanes have become fiercer and more frequent. The gap between the chapter and the headline is the object of study. T5: the 1940-1970 problem he highlights -- greenhouse-gas emissions rose steeply through those decades while global temperature did not, and models have to invoke aerosol cooling to reproduce it. A model that must be told the answer for one stretch is a model to be careful with for the next. T5: what Koonin CONCEDES, stated as loudly as what he disputes -- the climate is changing, CO2 warms, humans influence it; his own 2014 Wall Street Journal essay 'Climate Science Is Not Settled' put CO2-driven warming at roughly 0.04 degrees C per decade. His claim is about CERTAINTY and about the distance between reports and headlines, not about whether the greenhouse effect exists. A rung that turns him into a greenhouse-effect denier is simply false. T5: the number the whole argument turns on -- equilibrium climate sensitivity, the eventual warming from doubled CO2, has been quoted with a range of roughly 1.5 to 4.5 degrees C for over forty years, and the low and high ends imply very different centuries. Teach the term and the spread. T5: the 'red team' proposal and why it is a scientific idea, not a political one -- Koonin argued for a formal adversarial review of climate assessments, the practice used in intelligence analysis and engineering where a team is PAID to attack the conclusion. A discipline that will not fund its own attackers is trusting itself. T5: the sequel and its contested reception -- Koonin joined Stanford's Hoover Institution as Edward Teller Fellow in 2024, and in July 2025 co-authored a US Department of Energy review with John Christy, Judith Curry, Ross McKitrick and Roy Spencer arguing that US extreme-weather trends sit within historical variability and that climate sensitivity likely lies at the lower end of the quoted range. The report was contested on publication, and the bank says so in the same rung.
source: Grokipedia, 'Steven E. Koonin' (Caltech 1975, provost 1995-2004; BP chief scientist 2004-2009; DOE Under Secretary for Science 19 May 2009 to 18 November 2011 under Secretary Steven Chu, over five billion dollars annual science budget across ten national laboratories; the 19 September 2014 Wall Street Journal essay 'Climate Science Is Not Settled' with CO2-driven warming at about 0.04 C per decade and sensitivity quoted at 1.5-4.5 C; 'Unsettled' published 2021 by BenBella Books, expanded edition June 2024; red team/blue team proposals 2017-2019; Edward Teller Fellow at the Hoover Institution from 2024; co-authorship of the 23 July 2025 DOE report 'A Critical Review of Impacts of Greenhouse Gas Emissions on the U.S. Climate' with Christy, Curry, McKitrick and Spencer). Wikipedia, 'Steven E. Koonin' (the same career dates; the named published criticism of his 2014 essay). BenBella Books publisher page for 'Unsettled' (the claims listed as misleading -- surging seas, fiercer hurricanes, economic disaster -- the 1940-1970 temperature point, and the explicit statement that the climate IS changing). BUILD MUST READ the IPCC AR6 WG1 Summary for Policymakers directly for any confidence phrase or sensitivity range it quotes.
framing_note: vision_mandated -- this is the bank's declared MATURE view on climate, and its soul is METHOD rather than conclusions. The transferable move a kid can copy is 'go read the actual report, then compare it with the headline about the report'. Dinner-test payoff = the library-card method at T3/T4 (the most powerful climate tool in the book is reading the book). Accuracy rails, all load-bearing: (1) Koonin ACCEPTS that the climate is changing and that humans influence it -- any rung implying he denies the greenhouse effect is a factual error and a hard fail; (2) every claim attributed to him must be his actual claim with a source, and every IPCC confidence phrase must be QUOTED from the report rather than paraphrased; (3) the ladder must state that he has serious published critics and that the 2025 DOE review was contested -- the bank presents a defensible minority-of-experts position as exactly that, never as settled; (4) NO hagiography -- the answer to a rung is never 'Koonin is right', it is what he DID or what a document says. Anti-restatement: the stem gives the scene (a former Under Secretary sitting down with the assessment report itself) and the answer is the specific finding, recalled. Distractor mine = real adjacent figures across the whole spectrum (Judith Curry, John Christy, Roy Spencer, Richard Lindzen, Zeke Hausfather, Gavin Schmidt, Michael Mann) and real institutions (IPCC, NOAA, DOE, the National Climate Assessment). BANNED: the word 'denier', and any smug or triumphal framing. Lane border: PHILOSOPHY owns expertise and authority as an epistemology seminar; here the move is concrete and repeatable -- read the primary document.
history_overlap: science bank, howscience strand: the 'peer review is not a truth-detector' and 'institutional capture / revolving door' ladders make the general case -- this ladder keys ONLY the read-the-assessment-report method and Koonin's specific documented claims, and must not restate the general capture argument. This sub-strand's 'Prophecies with dates on them' ladder carries the Hausfather 2022 hot-model comment -- keep that fact in one ladder only.

name: The price tag and the private jet
scope: Where the physics stops and the politics starts -- named, dated, and reported flat. T3: France, autumn 2018 -- a scheduled increase in the carbon component of the fuel tax, falling hardest on diesel, put people wearing the high-visibility vests French drivers are required to carry into the streets from 17 November 2018. On 10 December 2018 President Macron announced the increase was cancelled. Nothing about the physics of CO2 changed that month; the politics did. T3/T4: Washington State, 2016 -- Initiative 732 proposed a revenue-neutral carbon tax starting at 15 dollars a tonne and rising to 100, paired with a cut in the state sales tax from 6.5 percent to 5.5 percent. It lost, 59 percent to 41. Part of the opposition came from environmental, environmental-justice and labour groups who objected not to taxing carbon but to giving the revenue BACK to taxpayers. The fight was over who got the money. T4: Davos -- an analysis of chartered aviation around the World Economic Forum's 2022 meeting counted over a thousand private-jet flights in and out of the airports serving Davos during the event week. The bank reports the count, names the analyst and the method, and adds no adjective. T4/T5: what the alarm does to children, measured -- Caroline Hickman and colleagues surveyed 10,000 people aged 16 to 25 across ten countries for The Lancet Planetary Health in 2021; close to 60 percent reported being very or extremely worried about climate change, and large fractions reported those feelings affecting their daily functioning. The bank treats this neither as proof the danger is fake nor as proof it is real: it is a measured effect of HOW the danger is communicated to children, and that is itself a fact worth knowing. T5: the word that ends arguments -- 'denier', borrowed from Holocaust denial, is applied to people who accept the greenhouse effect but dispute sensitivity, attribution or policy. A label that makes a person unaskable is not an argument, and the bank does not use it about anyone, in any stem, choice or context. T5: the real disagreement, named honestly -- the serious argument about carbon taxes is not whether CO2 absorbs infrared; it is about discount rates, damage functions and who bears the cost, and careful economists reach different numbers from the SAME physics. Naming the actual disagreement is more respectful than pretending there is none. T5: a check the reader can run -- every carbon policy announcement claims a tonnage effect. Ask what TEMPERATURE difference it claims to buy, and by when. Most announcements do not carry the number.

framing_note: vision_mandated, and the HIGHEST tone risk in the sub-strand -- treat every rung as a tripwire. The bank's lean is real (carbon taxes are political economy rather than neutral science; the alarm culture makes moral demands on children; 'denier' is a slur the bank never uses) but every rung must be a DOCUMENTED FACT with a date, delivered flat, with no adjective doing the argument's work. The words 'hypocrite' and 'cult' must not appear in the bank's own voice; the private-jet figure is reported as a COUNT and nothing more. Dinner-test payoff = Washington I-732, because 'environmental groups helped defeat a carbon tax' reorganizes a kid's entire mental map of the issue. Accuracy rails: (1) the Davos and Lancet rungs must be exactly sourced or DROPPED -- an unsourced number here would be the worst failure in this whole sub-strand; (2) a rung or its context must make explicit that the disagreement is over policy and sensitivity, never over whether CO2 absorbs infrared -- the ladder must not leave a kid thinking the physics is partisan; (3) the young people in the Lancet survey are the reader's own peers and must never be described with contempt. Distractor mine = real policy instruments (cap and trade, the EU Emissions Trading System, border carbon adjustments, feed-in tariffs, renewable portfolio standards) and real named actors and groups -- never joke options, never a cartoon villain.
